question_text: For any natural number k, let aₖ = 3ᵏ. The smallest natural number m for which (a₁)¹ × (a₂)² × ... × (a₂₀)²⁰ < (a₂₁ × a₂₂ × ... × a₂₀₊ₘ)⁵ is:
solution:
Given: aₖ = 3ᵏ.
Then (aᵢ)ⁱ = (3ᵢ)ⁱ = 3⁽ⁱ²⁾.
Left side:
L = (a₁)¹ × (a₂)² × ... × (a₂₀)²⁰ = 3^(1² + 2² + ... + 20²)
Sum of squares 1² + 2² + ... + 20² = 2870 → So L = 3²⁸⁷⁰.
Right side inside product:
P = a₂₁ × a₂₂ × ... × a₂₀₊ₘ = 3²¹ × 3²² × ... × 3^(20+m) = 3^(sum of integers from 21 to 20+m).
Raise to power 5: R = P⁵ = 3^(5 × sum of integers from 21 to 20+m)
We need → 3²⁸⁷⁰ < 3^(5 × sum)
So: 2870 < 5 × (sum of 21 to 20+m)
Let N = 20 + m.
Sum from 21 to N = (N(N+1))/2 − 210.
So: 2870 < 5 × [(N(N+1))/2 − 210]
Divide and simplify:
(N(N+1))/2 > 784 → N(N+1) > 1568
Check values:
39×40 = 1560 (too small)
40×41 = 1640 (works)
So the smallest N = 40.
Thus:
m = N − 20 = 40 − 20 = 20 → Final Answer: m = 20

We want to isolate √x on one side of the equation. To do that, we multiply both sides by a certain fraction, which is 1 ÷ (7 + 4√3).
We simplify this fraction by multiplying the numerator and denominator by its conjugate (which is 7 - 4√3) to get rid of the square root in the denominator.
After simplifying the fraction, we end up with √x times (7 - 4√3) on the left side of the equation.
On the right side, 64 is multiplied by the simplified fraction.
To continue simplifying, we distribute √x times (7 - 4√3) to get x times (7/2 - 2√3) on the left side.
Finally, we have x times (7/2 - 2√3) = 64 on the right side.
